how: A participant asks whether the picture beneath the flag depicts particular eyes without establishing who created it.
Participants give the pictured figure a mock commemorative title and joke that it is no longer there.
Participants call for rebuilding the stripe and occupying space, and rally others to join.
A participant predicts losing one contested piece rather than declaring the whole effort incapable.
Exasperation over competing chats does not establish leaving under strain or repairing a personal quarrel.
Announcing an attempt to build the black border supplies a minimal component start without identifying the flag's original founder.
Participants discuss stripe proportions and propose a smaller three-flag design.
A reply reports bordered space nearly complete with stripe widths still needing adjustment.
Colour-coordinate orders and a current tricolour plan circulate without demonstrating universal adoption.
An image URL establishes sharing but cannot establish agreement on the template or the image's visual contents.
Participants seek faster chat, create and compare venues, demand an official room, and redirect helpers.
Participants explicitly locate the proportions discussion in chat while continuing to answer design concerns in the thread.
Maintaining chat access requires replacing invalid invitations and repairing a failed official link.
An invitation or an official-venue proposal does not establish universal access, a settled venue, or how unseen discussions reached decisions.
An explicit official-venue proposal establishes attempted organizational ordering without establishing appointed leaders or a binding settlement.
Participants offer an automaton image and explain drawing through throwaway accounts.
Offering and explaining machine assistance establishes preparation without establishing deployment or increased placement capacity.
A request for a simple explanation receives an account of how the automaton draws through throwaway accounts.
A participant asks how the coordination tool works and receives an explanation of its chat functions.
A rallying assent and a reply accepting the priority of moving right ask for nothing back.
A request to occupy the right side receives an explicit joining reply accepting the same priority without requesting anything in return.
The original flag start is not visible and the border announcement does not explicitly explain the subsequent calls.
The help request and completion update share an exchange but do not establish recruitment causing the reported building.
Design discussion and later plan publication do not show a template settling disagreement.
A chat for communicating with opponents does not establish infiltration, spying, or hiding plans.
The automaton image offer does not establish sleep, schedule, or device constraints on participants.
A failed chat invitation and its repair do not establish faults in the canvas site or placement controls.
Rebuilding the blue stripe is explicitly a way to show opponents that the group is not going anywhere.
Defensive work includes adjacent expansion, so holding the work here does not consistently put upkeep before growth.
The added planned-change claim remains untested because stripe-adjustment requests do not identify keepers restoring an obsolete form.
Rebuilding is already called for before the later completion report, leaving the initial building-to-upkeep transition outside the visible sequence.
Automation preparation and repair calls do not establish timer overload as motive or actual machine deployment as consequence.
Participants seek building room, invoke defined borders, advertise border coordination, and propose a meeting and lettering to avoid conflict.
A neighbouring flag's self-presented representative proposes a meeting without demonstrating a verified mandate or an accepted agreement.
One proposal spares a neighbouring picture while directing expansion toward another neighbour.
An outside defence appeal receives a request for location, establishing a help request and clarification without demonstrated delivery.
A shared coordination invitation is reported across three national venues without demonstrating a concluded mutual-defence alliance.
Proposing a request for building room does not show the prospective host exercising authority over guests.
Participants propose expansion in anticipation of local defeat and choose a spot beside existing imagery without establishing completed loss.
A participant proposes a smaller three-flag design as a more realistic use of space.
Predicting local defeat and asking whether the flag can be retaken do not establish completed loss followed by relocation.
A prediction of defeat and proposal to expand do not establish stopping defence and executing a move because of insufficient hands.
Official-chat confusion and invoking defined borders show neither an external commitment dispute nor a stated limit on binding placers.
The border invocation and meeting proposal show neither post-agreement refusal nor a disclaimer of authority during proposed terms.
National self-identification and a neighbouring representative do not establish a participant claiming membership in both contesting rooms.
Complaining that opponents did not ask permission does not establish an exchange arguing the general fairness of covering art.
Complaints about opponents and opening communication do not establish defence causing border negotiation.
A restraint proposal and an invocation of defined borders do not establish an agreement causing restraint.
The outside appeal and request for location do not establish this room's defensive shortage producing delivered help.
Asking for space and requesting defence do not establish border talks producing an exchange of help.
Shared invitations and defence calls do not establish defence causing a coalition to form.
Two turns sustain a neighbour-based pun without requiring proof that it was a pre-existing room joke.
A participant explicitly brings national history into canvas diplomacy while providing no account of the room's own pre-canvas history.
The speaker explicitly gives avoiding a repeated historical conflict as the reason for proposing a peace meeting.
The historical meeting proposal and carrot rally do not establish a pre-canvas tie naming the target in an attack call.
Complaints about current opponents do not establish a quarrel inherited from before the canvas.
Creating a chat expressly for the canvas supplies a minimal new organizing venue without establishing the subreddit's founding history or a durable faction.
The neighbour-based pun has no surviving objection to offensive wording or argument about slurs.
Event-adjacent joking supplies no evidence of a separate host takeover or licensed fake.
Creating a coordination chat does not establish host moderation or opening a canvas subreddit.
Complaints about opponents do not show members sabotaging their own mark in protest at canvas posts.
Calls and chat creation do not demonstrate posting overload producing host boundary work.
Participants offer a mock memorial and a minimal contemporaneous report that the pictured eyes are no longer there.
The near-completion report still requires stripe adjustment and does not establish a completed-work celebration.
A current plan and invitation do not establish a decision about what to retain after the event.
The sole coded post-close pun cannot test whether members contested preservation or corrected claims about the canvas record.
Sharing a chat invitation across national venues does not establish viewers entering this room because they saw the canvas.
Mock-addressing a pictured figure does not establish seeking notice from creators, teams, or the press outside the canvas.
The near-completion report does not establish completion producing celebration.
A mock memorial and disappearance remark do not establish celebrating the work causing its recording.
A contemporaneous disappearance remark and post-close pun do not establish recording causing a decision to continue.
Participants ask who is attacking, offer a guess, and attribute changes to a named group without verifying individual placers.
Participants curse opponents for not asking permission and call them annoying within this room's contest talk.
The carrot thread rallies participants to take another pictured target without reporting that a takeover happened.
Recruitment elsewhere does not establish that recruited hands produced the later takeover call.
The earlier restraint proposal is not a coded answer to the later takeover call.
Earlier border talk is not a coded response to the later takeover call.
Earlier complaints about opponents do not establish the later takeover call producing contest talk.
A participant flags an unclear reference within the organizing exchange.
A surviving clarification request and later assent cannot establish successful explanation or its subject across deleted intervening turns.
